title: GHA executor router
description: The second HTTP surface in `gha-clone-server.rs`: the `gha-executor-router` binary (src/executor_router_service.rs `router`). It places fixed-profile build jobs across reviewed AWS and Hetzner executors. NOTE: `/builds/:id` is registered with Axum 0.7 `:id` syntax; this map uses the v2 `{id}` spelling, so the source comparison reports drift until the crate moves to Axum 0.8.

BuildRouteId.doc: A namespaced build id, `<executor>~<upstream job id>`. The executor is pinned into the id so status reads never fan out.

RouterReady.doc: 200 with an empty `readyExecutors` when execution is disabled; otherwise 200 only if at least one executor's /readyz probe succeeded, else 503.

RouterRouting.doc: Why the router never fails over after a POST: an ambiguous acceptance could duplicate work.

RouterBuildRequest.doc: The only body POST /builds accepts, per `validate_build_request` in src/executor_router.rs. Any other key is rejected. It is not declared as this route's `request` because the handler takes the raw `Bytes` body: the request bytes are content-bound to the assignment for duplicate detection.

requestId.doc: 1-256 chars of letters, digits, '.', ':', '_', '-'. Forwarded upstream unchanged.

healthz.summary: Liveness plus configured and enabled executor counts.

capabilities.summary: Placement policy, enabled executors, and the fail-closed coordination rules.

metrics.summary: Prometheus text exposition with a bounded provider label set.

submit_build.summary: Place one fixed-profile build on an executor and relay the upstream answer.
submit_build.doc: The body must match `RouterBuildRequest`, but it is not declared as `request` here: the handler takes raw `Bytes` so the exact bytes can be bound to the assignment record and a replayed `requestId` with different content answers 409 instead of being placed twice. The response is the upstream build server's JSON, relayed unchanged.

get_build.summary: Status of one placed build, read from the executor pinned in the id.
get_build.doc: The upstream build server's job record, relayed unchanged.
